question: Should art museums set targets to buy more work by the groups their collections have long left out?
answer: Yes. Collections built over centuries will not rebalance by chance; left alone, curators keep buying from the same networks. In 2020 the Baltimore Museum of Art bought only works by women for a year and had no trouble filling it with strong art. A target forces a search that habit never makes.
move: Whichever side you took, it turns on where the gap is best fixed.
ask: Where in my own choices would a simple target make me look beyond my usual circle?
counterpoint: No. Targets turn artists into categories and can make every purchase look like a quota, which hurts the artists they mean to help. Museums competing for the same few names also inflate their prices. The imbalance was made in schools, galleries and markets long ago; museums should fix it there, by funding training and shows.
reference: Baltimore Museum of Art, announcement of the 2020 Vision acquisitions initiative, November 2019
